title: Incrementable Min Stack
description:
Design a bounded stack `IncrementableMinStack` that supports adding a signed `delta` to the **bottom `k` elements** while answering `top` and `getMin` in **`O(log maxSize)` time**.

Implement the `IncrementableMinStack` class:
- `IncrementableMinStack(int maxSize)` initializes an empty stack with maximum capacity `maxSize`.
- `void push(int val)` pushes `val` onto the top of the stack if current size `< maxSize` (otherwise ignores the call).
- `long pop()` removes and returns the top element of the stack.
- `void increment(int k, int delta)` adds `delta` (positive, zero, or negative) to the **bottom `k` elements** of the stack (if fewer than `k` elements exist, updates all elements in the stack).
- `long top()` returns the current top element of the stack.
- `long getMin()` returns the current minimum element in the stack.
constraints: Methods pop, top, and getMin are always called on non-empty stacks.
At most 2 * 10^4 calls will be made across all methods.
hints: Unlike a plain increment stack, updating only the bottom `k` elements can change which index holds the global minimum.

Back the stack slots `[0..maxSize - 1]` with a lazy-propagation range-minimum segment tree: `push` performs a point-assign at `size` (pushing down stale lazy tags along the root-to-leaf path), `increment(k, delta)` performs a range-add on `[0, min(k, size) - 1]`, and `getMin()` queries range-min on `[0, size - 1]`.

examples.explanation: Pushing beyond maxSize 2 is ignored; incrementing k=5 affects all 2 existing elements.
Re-pushing into a previously popped slot overwrites its value cleanly without leaking old lazy offsets.
